systemic_signals.title: The warm-ink clause is a proven no-op; the ink is seeded, not prompted
systemic_signals.detail: All three frames carried an explicit, emphatic warm-ink instruction ('Every outline in the frame is drawn in the warm dark brown house ink, never a cool, grey-green or blue-black line'). Measured movement: L44 +0.1 -> +1.1, L46 +1.0 -> +2.1, L48 +0.03 -> +1.9. Against a +18 target that is noise. All three still read green-neutral (hue 117/102/116deg). Meanwhile every figure card feeding these frames is properly warm (+19.5, +41.8, +39.3) and the L28 place seed measures +3.0. The children track the SEED, not the cards and not the prose. Conclusion: ink register is inherited through the place-seed mechanism and prose cannot override it. The fix is to re-mint L28 with warm ink and re-seed its five children - not to keep adding ink language. Three frames is now enough evidence to stop trying the prose route.

systemic_signals.title: Content instructions land; chroma, scale and spatial-relation instructions do not
systemic_signals.detail: Clean split across the round. LANDED (all object-content): strip the rack to bare metal, draw the bucket blank, hang the fascia board, draw four digits, put him outside on tarmac, dress him in brown, match the room's surfaces, execute a slump. DID NOT LAND: 'kept small and muted in tone' (L32 bucket - red area moved 5%, saturation went UP), 'warm dark brown house ink' (x3, noise), 'palette gone colder' (L44 - median_sat bit-identical), 'the shaft BESIDE him, not on his body' (L48 - he is dead centre in the pool on a second, emphasised attempt), 'stage-LEFT' (L46 - 8% left of centre). Actionable: express correctives as objects and their states, never as tone, scale or relative position. Where a relative position is the beat, it needs a mechanism, not a stronger adjective.
